You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | US Stocks Fall for Third Session; Apple’s Foldable Starts at $1,999; Meta Rallies 6.55% (September 10, 2026)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve Dynamics
PPI arrives today as inflation faces scrutiny before the Fed meeting
The Federal Reserve meets on September 15–16 and will release a new Summary of Economic Projections.
Higher energy costs complicate the inflation outlook. Incoming data will help shape market expectations for the Fed’s next policy decision.
US August PPI is due today at 20:30 Beijing time, followed by CPI tomorrow at the same time, providing fresh evidence before next week’s meeting.
Market Impact : The immediate question for technology stocks and crypto assets is whether inflation data will justify a less restrictive rate outlook. Persistent price pressure could keep borrowing costs and valuation discount rates elevated; softer data would give risk appetite a firmer basis for recovery.
International Commodities
EIA sees continued inventory drawdowns, keeping oil supply risks in focus
The EIA’s September 9 outlook estimates that global oil inventories have fallen by approximately 400 million barrels this year and will continue declining through the end of 2026.
The agency forecasts average Brent spot prices of approximately $91 per barrel in 2026 and $74 in 2027. These are annual forecasts, conditional on supply gradually recovering.
The EIA expects some constraints on Middle Eastern oil exports to persist through year-end, with regional production remaining below pre-conflict averages until the second quarter of 2027.
Market Impact : Tight supply supports the earnings outlook for oil producers while increasing cost pressure on transport and manufacturing. For the broader market, the key question is how far energy costs spread into other prices and constrain central banks’ room to ease policy.
Macroeconomic Policy
Treasury sets a $6 billion buyback ceiling, but bonds remain under pressure
The US Treasury announced that its September 10 operation will repurchase up to $6 billion of nominal Treasury securities with 10–20 years remaining to maturity.
The operation is scheduled for September 11, 01:40–02:00 Beijing time. The $6 billion figure is the maximum permitted amount, not a commitment to purchase that amount.
Treasury securities sold off after the announcement as the size fell short of some investors’ expectations, leaving the market focused on whether the operation can improve liquidity.
Market Impact : Buybacks can improve trading conditions in older securities, but their effect on longer-term financing costs depends on the bond market’s response. AI infrastructure businesses, property and other capital-intensive sectors remain sensitive to sustained increases in long-term borrowing costs.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex Performance
Spot gold : Approximately $4,396.73 per ounce.
Spot silver : Approximately $67.29 per ounce.
WTI crude oil futures : Indicative price of approximately $96.61 per barrel, October 2026 contract.
Brent crude oil futures : Indicative price of approximately $101.37 per barrel, November 2026 contract.
US Dollar Index (DXY) : Approximately 98.80.
Driver Analysis : Brent remains above $100 as supply disruptions and inventory drawdowns sustain the market’s focus on energy security. Gold is trading around $4,400, with safe-haven demand competing against interest-rate pressure. Today’s PPI release and ECB decision are the next catalysts for currencies and precious metals.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC : Approximately 78,205.01 USDT , down 0.65% over 24 hours.
ETH : Approximately 2,467.70 USDT, down 1.08% over 24 hours.
Total cryptocurrency market capitalization : Approximately $2.75 trillion.
Driver Analysis : Both major assets declined over the past 24 hours, with ETH underperforming BTC. Upcoming US inflation data and the Treasury buyback are the immediate macro catalysts. Next week’s expected procedural vote on the CLARITY Act adds a regulatory regulatory event to watch, although progress toward a vote alone does not establish sustained buying demand.
US Equity Index Performance
Dow Jones : Closed at 52,380.66, down 0.77%.
S&P 500 : Closed at approximately 7,636, down 0.48%.
Nasdaq Composite : Closed at 26,253.34, down 0.64%.
Tech Giants Dynamics
NVDA : $223.67, down 0.91%.
AAPL : $315.34, down 0.28%.
MSFT : $491.65, down 0.47%.
GOOGL : $330.65, down 2.28%.
AMZN : $252.40, down 1.78%.
META : $653.69, up 6.55%.
TSLA : $367.81, down 0.10%.
Performance Summary & Driver Analysis : Using Alphabet’s Class A shares, six of the seven tech giants declined. Meta was the clear outperformer following its Muse AI agent launch, while Alphabet and Amazon led the declines. Apple slipped despite unveiling its foldable iPhone, with pricing and margins under scrutiny. The divergence highlights the market’s selective response to company catalysts amid pressure on the broader indices, with AI application monetization and hardware cost pressures emerging as distinct trading themes.
Sector Movers Observation
[...]
AI applications: Meta’s agent launch puts monetization in focus
[...]
Representative stock : Meta (META) rose 6.55%.
[...]
Drivers : Following the September 8 launch of Muse, investors are assessing whether an agent that performs tasks across apps can turn Meta’s AI spending into new revenue. The next evidence will come from adoption, retention and paid conversion.
[...]
1. Apple (AAPL) - Foldable iPhone arrives; pricing puts margins to the test
[...]
Event Overview : Apple fell 0.28% on September 9, closing at $315.34. Its first foldable iPhone, Duo, starts at $1,999 in the US and RMB15,999 in mainland China. Preorders are scheduled to open on October 16, with availability from October 23; the mainland China launch remains subject to approval. The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max start at $1,199 and $1,299, respectively.
[...]
Market Interpretation : Bloomberg Intelligence estimates first-year Duo shipments of approximately 14 million units. Jefferies, however, warns that Apple’s pricing strategy could sacrifice margins to support volumes. A higher-end product mix could help revenue, but component costs, production yields and the extent of genuinely incremental demand will determine the profit contribution.
[...]
2. Meta (META) - A 6.55% rally shifts attention to AI agent monetization
[...]
Event Overview : Meta rose 6.55% on September 9, closing at $653.69. The move followed the September 8 launch of Muse, a personal AI agent initially available in the US through a dedicated app and WhatsApp, designed to carry out tasks such as sending emails and booking travel.
[...]
Market Interpretation : The agent gives Meta a new opportunity to monetize AI beyond advertising. The investment case now depends on whether users adopt it consistently and pay for useful services. Reliability, permission controls and the cost of completing tasks will influence both trust and profitability.
[...]
In commentary reported on September 10, Moody’s chief economist Mark Zandi warned that politically driven rate cuts could lead bond investors to question the Fed’s independence and expect higher inflation, pushing up long-term rates and borrowing costs for businesses and commercial property. In its post-launch Apple commentary, Jefferies warned that the company could sacrifice some margin to support sales. The former highlights the cost of weakened policy credibility; the latter emphasizes the trade-off between product sales and profitability.
